keyField.description:
Key field to use for partitioning.  Note the following:

1. Currently only single field partitioning is supported.
2. Only fields that store their values in a single column as a "truly" primitive value (e.g. NOT json) are allowed

strategy.description: Indicates which type of partitioning will be used (e.g. `range` or `list`).

partitions.description:
Map of partition values to use, specified as a comma separated list in a single string, keyed by the partition
name.  Note that for `list` partitions, every value will be, explicitly part of the partition.

For 'range' partitions, The values must contain only 2 entries, the first being the minimum (inclusive) value for
the partition and the second being the maximum (exclusive) value for the partition.  For range partitions, the
partition configurations must be non-overlapping and cover all possible expected values.  Otherwise, errors will
occur when creating the partitions or writing to the database.

Note the following:

1. The values should be specified as strings and must be naturally convertible to the appropriate data type for
   the underlying column for the field (e.g. '2021-12-01' for a date or dateTime field).

title:
Defines the partition structure for a persistable type's partitioned database table in Postgres.  Details for
Postgres partitioning can be found at:

`https://www.postgresql.org/docs/12/ddl-partitioning.html`

Note the following limitations:

1. Only `list` and `range` partitioning are supported at this time.
2. Since a true primary key index can not span multiple tables, it is a requirement in Postgres that the primary key
   defined for a partitioned table must include the partition key column, we will enforce the KV strategy for our
   `id` field (e.g. "<partitionKey>#<unique value in partition>") to facilitate the correct upsert behavior and to
   ensure that there are not "duplicate" ids returned from fetch/get.
3. No other unique indexes will be supported for partitioned tables.
4. Since there is no effective way to have matching partitioning for child collection tables for a partitioned table,
   no non-fkey child collections will be allowed.
5. Changes to the partition key field's value will not be permitted.


ALSO NOTE! The above description may change as the POC progresses.
